text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared central repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project to combine everyone’s work, each change is automatically verified through a CI pipeline. This pipeline typically starts with an automated build, which compiles the code and packages it for deployment. Immediately after, a suite of automated tests runs against the build. These tests check for bugs, performance problems, and integration errors. The main advantage is catching issues early in the development cycle, when they are cheaper and easier to fix. If a test fails, the team is notified instantly, so problems are solved quickly, keeping the software stable and reliable.
